clue.text: 20% cider guzzled by drunk northerner

indicators.note: something guzzled by a drinker goes inside them, so the letter sits within the drunk

parts.note: a sot is a habitual drunk

indicators.note: one fifth of a five-letter word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A tipsy man downs a fairly strong cider.
explanation.walkthrough: '20%' of the five letters of 'cider' is one letter, C, which goes inside SOT.
explanation.definitionFit: A Scot comes from Scotland, in the far north of Britain, so is a northerner.

clue.text: Country is leaving Europe after Remain leaders retire

indicators.note: to retire is to go back, so the picked letters run backwards
the leaders of the four words are their opening letters, taken together

explanation.surface: A Brexit-flavoured line: a country quits the EU once the Remain camp's leading figures step down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Remain' and 'leaving' look like Brexit politics, but they are just words whose initials are taken, with 'retire' turning that run backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Israel is a nation state in the Middle East.

clue.text: Old man, eternal and enigmatic

indicators.note: something enigmatic is puzzling and jumbled, so the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: An ancient figure is described as everlasting and mysterious.
explanation.definitionFit: Neandertal man is an extinct early human, so an old kind of man in an evolutionary sense.

clue.text: In the outskirts of Banbury, cat wants tail to be like Tigger?

indicators.note: the cut-down cat sits in the edges of the town's name
the outskirts of a word are its first and last letters
lacking its tail means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: an ounce is the snow leopard, a big cat

explanation.surface: A cat around the edge of the Oxfordshire town of Banbury loses its tail and wants to be like Winnie-the-Pooh's friend.
explanation.walkthrough: The ounce, or snow leopard, is a crossword favourite for 'cat'; Banbury is a town in Oxfordshire.
explanation.definitionFit: Tigger, the tiger in Winnie-the-Pooh, is famous for bouncing, so springy and lively describes him.

clue.text: Guy tackles poorly, giving up a small score

indicators.note: done poorly, the letters end up in a muddled order
giving up means these letters are left out of the mixed pool

explanation.surface: A footballer named Guy tackles badly and concedes a modest scoreline.
explanation.walkthrough: Mix GUYTACKLES, drop the A and S ('giving up a small'), and what remains rearranges to the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To score is slang for a romantic or sexual success, the same idiom as succeeding with a date.

clue.text: Painter's first dog was a boxer

definitions.note: read as 'painter is', the contraction joining definition to wordplay

indicators.note: the first of a word is its opening letter

parts.note: Muhammad Ali was a heavyweight boxer

explanation.surface: An artist's earliest pet dog was a boxer breed.
explanation.definitionFit: Salvador Dalí was the Spanish surrealist painter.

clue.text: England midfielder can play with English league

parts.note: Dele Alli played in midfield for England

indicators.note: letters at play move freely, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: An England midfielder is able to turn out with an English football league side.
explanation.definitionFit: An alliance and a league are both unions of parties for a shared purpose.

clue.text: One agreement or many?

definitions.note: the plural, many votes in favour, with the question mark flagging the stretch

parts.note: a is the indefinite article, meaning one
yes expresses agreement

explanation.surface: A question whether this is a single agreement or several.
explanation.walkthrough: Ayes are votes in favour; one would be an aye, so 'many' asks for the plural.
explanation.definitionFit: In parliament the votes in favour are counted as a plural, so many assenting votes.

clue.text: 1960s' Mama's key function? To make stew

parts.note: Mama Cass Elliot sang with the 1960s group the Mamas and the Papas
E is a musical key
a role is a function or job

explanation.surface: A puzzle about a 1960s singer's musical key, ending with a cookery instruction.
explanation.definitionFit: To casserole food is to cook it slowly in liquid in a covered dish, which is stewing it.

clue.text: Friend embraces European way

indicators.note: to embrace is to hold inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: an ally is a friend

explanation.surface: A friend gives a hug to a European along the road.
explanation.definitionFit: An alley is a narrow lane, a kind of way or passage.

clue.text: Labour ousting leader leads to succession

indicators.note: ousting the leader drops the opening letter

parts.note: strain is labour or toil

explanation.surface: The Labour Party pushes out its leader, prompting a question of who comes next.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Labour' looks like the party but is a verb or noun for effort.
explanation.definitionFit: A train of events is a series, one following another.

clue.text: Abolishes work in full? That's the origin of socialism

indicators.note: worked letters are reshaped into a new order

parts.note: i.e. is short for id est, that is

indicators.note: the origin of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A political line: abolition done thoroughly is the root of socialism.
explanation.walkthrough: 'work' rearranges IN FULL to NULLIF; 'That's' gives IE, and S begins 'socialism'.
explanation.definitionFit: To nullify something is to cancel it, which is abolishing it.

clue.text: The gods are 60% angry about everybody taking ecstasy

indicators.note: one piece wraps about the other
three-fifths of a five-letter word is its last three letters
everybody takes the drug on board, the one following the other

parts.note: all means everybody
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: The gods are cross that everyone is on ecstasy.
explanation.walkthrough: 60% of ANGRY is GRY, which goes round ALLE.
explanation.definitionFit: The gods is theatre slang for the highest balcony, the upper gallery.

clue.text: Suggestion of grand crowd …

parts.note: G is short for grand, a thousand pounds
a host is a great crowd

explanation.surface: A hint of a great throng, trailing into the next clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A ghost of something is a faint trace or hint of it.

clue.text: Count change on firm palm

indicators.note: in a down-style reading, one piece placed on another; here the jumbled word follows

parts.note: CO is short for company, a firm

indicators.note: to change letters is to rearrange them

explanation.surface: An accountant tallies money on the hand of a firm.
explanation.definitionFit: The coconut palm is the tropical tree that bears the coconut.

clue.text: … holding party lessons right away …

parts.note: Con is short for the Conservative Party

indicators.note: with right away, the R is removed

parts.note: training is a course of lessons

explanation.surface: A chain of clues: a party's lessons take place directly.
explanation.definitionFit: Something containing an item is holding it within.

clue.text: … belonging to the Irish?

definitions.note: a possessive, owned by those people

parts.note: taken as written; that the letters also run through 'the Irish' unbroken is a coincidence of this charade

explanation.surface: The chain ends asking what belongs to the people of Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: This possessive word marks something as owned by a group of people already mentioned.

clue.text: Rolling stones have no end of moss at the beginning

indicators.note: letters rolling about tumble into a new order
having none of a letter means it is taken out
the end of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: A twist on the proverb that a rolling stone gathers no moss.
explanation.walkthrough: STONES minus S (end of 'moss') is STONE, which 'Rolling' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: The onset of something is its start.

clue.text: Firing honest, outstanding intellectuals often ends disastrously

indicators.note: a disastrous outcome leaves things scrambled, so the letters are mixed
the ends of each word are its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Sacking upright, brilliant thinkers usually turns out badly.
explanation.walkthrough: The ends give HT, OG, IS, ON, which 'disastrously' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: Firing a gun is the act of discharging shots.

clue.text: Reserved "special" with hungry, empty stomach

indicators.note: a word with an empty stomach loses its insides, keeping its outer letters

explanation.surface: A quiet person, self-styled as special, goes hungry.
explanation.definitionFit: A shy person is reserved and keeps to themselves.

clue.text: Rector wears belt, plus diamonds and vestment

indicators.note: the clergyman's letter is worn inside the jumbled letters
to belt is to beat, so the letters are knocked into a new order

parts.note: ice is slang for diamonds

explanation.surface: A vicar dresses in a belt, jewels and robes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'belt' looks like the clothing in the scene but works as the scrambling signal, meaning to beat.
explanation.definitionFit: A surplice is the loose white linen robe worn by clergy and choristers.

clue.text: Relative not against touring Venice

indicators.note: the letters going on tour move about into a new order
not means the letter is left out

parts.note: V for versus means against

explanation.surface: A family member who doesn't mind visiting Venice.
explanation.walkthrough: VENICE without V is ENICE, which 'touring' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: A niece, a sibling's daughter, is a relative.

clue.text: One taking a gentle walk doffs hat to fisherman

indicators.note: doffing the hat removes the top letter

parts.note: a stroller is someone ambling

explanation.surface: A walker raises their hat to someone fishing.
explanation.definitionFit: A troller fishes by trailing a baited line behind a moving boat.

clue.text: Mat's a freewheeler

definitions.meaning: a small mat set under a drink, with the contraction joining the two senses
someone who glides along, as a cyclist coasting downhill

explanation.surface: A man named Mat is a carefree type.
explanation.definitionFit: Both a drinks mat and someone who coasts along without effort share this one word.

clue.text: Keep those who play with the French

parts.note: the cast are the actors in a play
le is French for the

explanation.surface: Keep the actors who perform alongside the French troupe.
explanation.definitionFit: A keep is the fortified central tower of a castle, so the two name the stronghold.

clue.text: I can't recycle new container

indicators.note: recycled material is reworked, so these letters are reshaped

explanation.surface: Someone protests they cannot recycle a fresh container.
explanation.definitionFit: A metal food tin is a common container for preserved food.

clue.text: Tom and Paul excited by Troy's siege weapons

parts.note: a tom is a male cat

indicators.note: excited letters jump about into a new arrangement

parts.note: t is the abbreviation for troy weight, followed by the possessive s

explanation.surface: Two men thrilled by the war machines at Troy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tom' is not a name here but a male cat; troy is the system of weights used for precious metals.
explanation.definitionFit: Catapults hurled stones at the walls of besieged towns.

clue.text: Port served at 1:00 or 10:00, going by the numbers?

parts.note: read as the number 100, it is the Roman numeral C
read as the number 1000, it is K, short for kilo or thousand

explanation.surface: A port wine served at one o'clock or ten o'clock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going by the numbers' tells you to read the times as plain numbers, 100 and 1000, without the colon.
explanation.definitionFit: Cork is a harbour city in southern Ireland, a port.

clue.text: Writer has time for another

indicators.note: the writer has the letter added after him

parts.note: Edgar Allan Poe was an American writer

explanation.surface: An author finds time for another book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'another' is another writer, carrying on from 'Writer'.
explanation.definitionFit: A poet is a writer of verse, so another kind of writer.

clue.text: Man in Japan bit assassin

indicators.note: a bit of the phrase is a stretch of its letters

explanation.surface: A man in Japan bites a hired killer.
explanation.definitionFit: A ninja was a Japanese covert agent trained in assassination.

clue.text: F1 driver not performing as well

indicators.note: not means the letters are left out

parts.note: Fernando Alonso is a Formula One driver
on means performing, on stage

explanation.surface: A racing driver isn't doing as well.
explanation.definitionFit: Also and as well are synonyms meaning in addition.

clue.text: Distance to mountains

definitions.meaning: the reach or extent something covers

explanation.surface: How far it is to the hills.
explanation.definitionFit: This word means both the reach of a weapon and a line of mountains.

clue.text: Records, say, see Arsenal dribbling around D

indicators.note: say signals that the word is spoken, giving the letter of the same sound

parts.note: spoken, the word matches the letter C

indicators.note: the mixed letters go around the D
a footballer dribbling weaves about, so the letters move

explanation.surface: Records show the London football club Arsenal dribbling round a defender.
explanation.definitionFit: Calendars are registers or schedules of dates, records in that sense.
